messages:
Alex K: incident-bot alerted p95/p99 spike on prod-inference at 10:04 UTC, paging oncall
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: latency.p99 > 2.0s on route /v1/generate (threshold 1.2s) — firing (alert id: A-19725-latency)
Maya S: oncall paging? who is on today
sre-pager: @alex.k you're the primary until 10:45, @james.l is secondary
Alex K: ack, I'm on it. Initial glance — graphs look like a sudden jump starting ~10:02. p95 -> 1.4s, p99 -> 2.3s. Streaming tails show stalls @tail nodes
James L: is this global or region-specific? any error volume increase?
Alex K: looks US-west heavy. Error rate stable +0.1% (noise). But inflight streaming connections show backlog — long tail of websocket ack delays.
Lia T: putting oncall Huddle: https://meet.redwood.internal/h/latency-triage-19725
Alex K: attaching quick checks
```
# k8s: check pods
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep ready
# gw: qps/latency
curl -s "https://dashboards.redwood.internal/api/query?panel=latency&route=/v1/generate"
```
Alex K: pods look healthy, no CrashLoop. Node CPU/GPU fine. Network Rx spiky on node-gw-7
Maya S: can you post the dashboard links (panels) — want to see per-model breakdown
Alex K: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/rl-inference/latency-overview?org=redwood&var-route=/v1/generate
https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/rl-inference/model-split?var-region=us-west
Alex K: model-split shows 80% traffic hitting model-16q at us-west1, where p99 is 2.6s
James L: is there a hot prefix/large-context causing kv cache misses? recent customer traffic pattern changes?
Alex K: quick grep of logs for long contexts shows a small subset of requests with >4k tokens from a partner integration
Lia T: customer impact? any paid users complaining / errors?
Alex K: no errors. Increased latency only. Estimated impacted requests ~3% of prod qps, but top-10 customers show 12% of their requests delayed. Flagging customer: partner-acme
incident-bot: paging: Severity S2 — service impaired, partial impact. Use #pager-duty for urgent escalations.
Maya S: propose mitigation 1) divert new requests in us-west to a lower-latency model variant (model-8q) 2) enable prefix cache for large-context route 3) temporary rate-limit partner-acme if they don't cooperate
James L: can we route by model variant automatically? what's weight change command?
Alex K: routing command (console API):
```
POST /api/v1/routes/route123/traffic
{"variant_weights": {"model-16q":0.3, "model-8q":0.7}}
```
Alex K: issuing traffic shift now to 70% model-8q for us-west only. Applying canary at 10:17
deploy-bot: traffic update accepted, rollout id r-19725-01, canary 70% -> model-8q in region us-west
James L: monitoring p95/p99 now
Alex K: p95 dropped to 0.9s within 90s, p99 to 1.4s. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated (some tail ~1.8s)
Lia T: good. Can you add a temporary caching rule for /v1/generate prefix segments for partner-acme? Ops-runbook suggests enabling prefix/KV cache with 30s TTL
Alex K: added cache rule for partner-acme with 60s TTL at 10:22
incident-bot: note: cache rule applied by Alex K (rule id c-19725-acme)
Maya S: what's the rollback if model-8q causes regressions in quality? any evals failing?
Alex K: quick evals show minor degradation on Rouge for that customer's prompts (delta -0.4%); we'll keep canary at 70% and watch quality signals in Optimize.
James L: any downstream SLOs for streaming clients? need to update incident page and notify CS
Alex K: creating incident doc — https://incidents.redwood.internal/19725-latency-paging
Alex K: @lia.t can you draft customer outreach for partner-acme? mention we're mitigating and may request short context trimming
Lia T: on it, will ping CS and AMs. Draft ETA 30m for follow-up
Maya S: do we need to spin up extra gw nodes in us-west? autoscaler shows capacity headroom but network queueing suggests transient net issue
Alex K: starting a controlled scale-up of gw pool +2 nodes at 10:28
deploy-bot: autoscaler initiated scale up: +2 gw nodes (scale id s-19725-gw)
Alex K: after scale up and routing change, p95 0.85s, p99 1.1s, streaming tails mostly cleared. Marking mitigation effective at 10:35
incident-bot: summary update: Mitigations applied: traffic reroute -> model-8q (canary 70%), prefix caching for partner-acme, gw pool +2 nodes. Latency trending down. Severity remains S2 while monitoring.
James L: moving to watch mode. I'll take notes for postmortem — need timeline, root cause hypotheses (hot large-context traffic + regional network queueing), and RCA owners
Alex K: +1. I'll stay until 11:00 then handoff to @james.l. Lia will handle customer comms
Lia T: customer outreach sent to partner-acme, they acknowledged and will throttle a heavy job. CS informed.
Maya S: thanks team. If anything spikes, escalate S1. Otherwise we'll close when stable for 60m
Alex K: last check 10:45: p95 0.8s, p99 1.05s, errors none. Handoff: @james.l, thread pinned to incident doc
James L: ack taking over. will collect logs and schedule postmortem. closing huddle but keeping thread open.
incident-bot: incident updated at 10:46 UTC — responder Alex K -> James L. Channel: #incidents
Alex K: signing off from oncall for this thread at 10:50, good job :thumbsup:
James L: thanks, I'll follow up with RCA draft by EOD.
